content: Beer potomania is a condition characterized by the development of hyponatremia, which refers to abnormally low sodium levels in the bloodstream. This condition arises due to excessive beer consumption combined with inadequate nutritional intake. It is a syndrome that involves binge drinking, poor dietary habits, and severe hyponatremia. The pathophysiology of beer potomania can be explained through an example. Consider an individual who consumes 4 liters of beer in a single day. Since beer is primarily water, this equates to ingesting 4 liters of water along with approximately 200 milliosmoles (mOsm) of solutes. For context, a typical American diet provides about 750 mOsm of solutes per day, all of which are excreted in the urine to maintain a steady state. In this scenario, the individual’s antidiuretic hormone (ADH) secretion is at its lowest level. ADH is the hormone responsible for promoting water reabsorption in the kidneys. When ADH secretion is minimized, the kidneys are able to excrete maximally dilute urine. The kidneys can achieve a maximum urine dilution of 50 mOsm/L. Therefore, to excrete the 200 mOsm of solutes consumed in the diet, the kidneys will produce 4 liters of urine (50 mOsm/L × 4 L = 200 mOsm). This process allows the individual to maintain normal sodium levels. However, if this same individual consumes a 5th liter of beer without ingesting any additional solutes, the kidneys will no longer be able to excrete the excess free water effectively. This results in a dilution of sodium levels in the bloodstream, leading to hyponatremia. This condition is referred to as beer potomania. In terms of diagnosis, laboratory findings play a critical role. A urine osmolality (Uosm) value of less than 100 mOsm/kg is indicative of complete and appropriate suppression of ADH secretion. This finding is commonly observed in cases of primary polydipsia, which includes beer potomania, or in conditions such as a reset osmostat.
